title: ArsalanZ/Nenya-2.5B-A0.5B-Base · Hugging Face
excerpt: Text Generation model with 3B parameters. Download, explore files and run it on Hugging Face.
content_html:
Model overview

Nenya is a general purpose 0.5B active, 2.5B total parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) base model. Nenya rivals Qwen3.5 2B on pretraining benchmarks with 500× lower training compute and 3.4× fewer active FLOPs/token.

Architecture Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)
Total Parameters 2.59B
Activated Parameters 553M
Routed-Expert Parameters 1.59B
Engram Table Parameters 528M
Number of Layers 32
Number of Dense Layers 2 (blocks 0–1)
Attention-Layer Composition 23 (GDN-2) + 9 (MLA)
Attention Hidden Dimension 960
Number of Attention Heads 12
Dense FFN Hidden Dimension 2560 (SwiGLU)
Latent MoE Dimension 384
MoE Hidden Dimension (per Expert) 384
Number of Experts 120
Selected Experts per Token 6
Number of Shared Experts 2
Expert Routing quantile-balanced
Residual Streams 4
Vocabulary Size 100,278
Padding Rows 74
Context Length 16,384
Attention Mechanism GDN-2 & MLA
Activation Function SwiGLU
Precision bf16
Modality Text

Quickstart

Any device with transformers:

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu"
repo = "ArsalanZ/Nenya-2.5B-A0.5B-Base"
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo, trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(repo, trust_remote_code=True, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(device)

inputs = tok("The mitochondrion is the organelle responsible for", return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=40)     # samples: temperature 0.9, top-k 20 (the default)
print(tok.decode(out[0], skip_special_tokens=True))

# maths, code and short factual answers: greedy decoding
out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=40, do_sample=False)

Any device with PyPI

Install it with pip install "nenya[cuda]" on NVIDIA GPUs to get the flash-linear-attention kernels and pip install "nenya" otherwise. With the pip package, trust_remote_code is not needed:

import torch
import nenya                                    # registers the model with transformers
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu"
repo = "ArsalanZ/Nenya-2.5B-A0.5B-Base"
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(repo, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(device)

On a Mac with Apple silicon, use the Metal engine for maximum throughput:

pip install "nenya[mac]"

import nenya
print(nenya.generate("The mitochondrion is the organelle responsible for", max_new_tokens=40))
print(nenya.generate("Question: What is the capital of Australia?\nAnswer:", max_new_tokens=8, temperature=0))

It runs on the Mac's GPU, about 125 tok/s on an M4, and downloads its 3.5 GB weight file on first use. It samples with the model's defaults (temperature 0.9, top-k 20); temperature=0 is greedy decoding, for maths, code and short factual answers.

  • Kernels: on NVIDIA GPUs, install flash-linear-attention (the cuda extra, or pip install flash-linear-attention) so the GDN-2 layers run on its Triton kernels. Without it, on a CPU, or through transformers on a Mac, they run a pure-PyTorch recurrence: same results, much slower, especially on long prompts.
  • Precision: use bf16, as it was trained and evaluated in. fp32 also works.

Evaluation

Pretraining Benchmarks

Scored with lm-evaluation-harness 0.4.13 through transformers (--model hf), from log-likelihoods only: no task generates text. Every model runs with the same settings:

  • bf16 weights, fp32 log-softmax, 4,096-token windows
  • zero-shot except TriviaQA (5-shot, otherwise Qwen's think token invalidates results), lm-eval's default seeds
  • the reference models at their pinned commits

Our training data was decontaminated against these benchmarks' evaluation sets.

Four tasks are ours, and their files are in this repo under evaluation/lm_eval_tasks:

  • mmlu_cloze: lm-eval's 57 mmlu_*_continuation tasks, grouped so that the pooled acc_norm is reported. The stock group reports only acc.
  • csqa_cloze
  • triviaqa_5shot_greedy
  • uncheatable_2026_07

Accuracies are in %, ± one standard error.

  • TriviaQA: 5-shot, on a fixed 4,000-question subset of the validation set. A question counts as right if greedy decoding reproduces any accepted alias, checked from log-likelihoods without generating. The examples show the short-answer format, so models that otherwise answer in sentences or <think> blocks (Qwen3.5 Base) are measured on knowledge.

UncheatableEval, July 2026 (bits per byte, lower is better)

The text was first published 1–25 July 2026 (Jellyfish042/UncheatableEval-2026-07), after every compared model's training data. Each category has 500 documents, each scored as a whole after the model's document-start token, in 4,096-token windows. Each group's average is the plain mean of its categories.

English (3 categories) 0.815 0.788 0.911 0.833 0.745 0.741

Code: GitHub (5 categories) 0.637 0.676 0.578 0.505 0.500 0.507

Code and maths (bits per byte of the reference solution, lower is better)

lm-eval scores GSM8K, MBPP and HumanEval only by generating answers. These rows come from the in-repo harness (pretraining/benchmarks.py, context 1,024): the reference models in fp32 with TF32 matmuls, this model in bf16.

Verify our results

The custom task files ship in this repo. On a CUDA GPU:

# our runs: torch 2.11.0+cu128 on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, datasets 5.0.1, huggingface_hub 1.33.0
pip install "lm-eval[hf]==0.4.13" "transformers==5.18.0" "torch==2.11.0" "flash-linear-attention==0.5.2" \
    "datasets==5.0.1"
hf download ArsalanZ/Nenya-2.5B-A0.5B-Base --include "evaluation/*" --local-dir nenya_eval
TASKS=nenya_eval/evaluation/lm_eval_tasks
ARGS=pretrained=ArsalanZ/Nenya-2.5B-A0.5B-Base,trust_remote_code=True,dtype=bfloat16,softmax_dtype=float32,max_length=4096
lm_eval --model hf --model_args $ARGS --include_path $TASKS --output_path results \
    --batch_size 32 --tasks hellaswag,arc_easy,arc_challenge,winogrande,piqa,sciq,openbookqa,lambada_openai,xstorycloze_en,csqa_cloze
lm_eval --model hf --model_args $ARGS --include_path $TASKS --output_path results \
    --batch_size 16 --tasks mmlu_cloze
lm_eval --model hf --model_args $ARGS --include_path $TASKS --output_path results \
    --batch_size 32 --tasks triviaqa_5shot_greedy
lm_eval --model hf --model_args $ARGS --include_path $TASKS --output_path results \
    --batch_size 2 --tasks uncheatable_2026_07

To score a reference model, set ARGS to its arguments below followed by ,dtype=bfloat16,softmax_dtype=float32,max_length=4096. Qwen3.5, Gemma 4 and SmolLM3 ran at half these batch sizes (their vocabularies are 128k–262k tokens). bf16 scores can move slightly with the GPU and the batch size.

Limitations

  • A base model. It continues text, it does not follow instructions, and it can produce false, biased or unsafe content.
  • Trained mostly on English web, educational, academic, code and maths data.
  • Quality past 16,384 tokens is untested. With no positional encoding there is no hard limit.

License

Apache 2.0: see LICENSE. NOTICE lists the third-party material: nenya_gdn2.py is derived from flash-linear-attention (MIT), and the tokenizer files come from allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct (Apache 2.0).

content_html_zh:
Model overview

Nenya is a general purpose 0.5B active, 2.5B total parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) base model. Nenya rivals Qwen3.5 2B on pretraining benchmarks with 500× lower training compute and 3.4× fewer active FLOPs/token.

建筑学 混合专家 (MoE)
总参数 2.59B
激活参数 553M
Routed-Expert Parameters 1.59B
Engram Table Parameters 528M
层数 32
致密层数 2 (blocks 0–1)
注意力层组成 23 (GDN-2) + 9 (MLA)
注意隐藏维度 960
注意力头数量 12
Dense FFN Hidden Dimension 2560 (SwiGLU)
潜在MoE维度 384
MoE 隐藏维度（每位专家） 384
专家人数 120
每个代币选定的专家 6
共享专家数量 2
Expert Routing quantile-balanced
Residual Streams 4
词汇量 100,278
Padding Rows 74
上下文长度 16,384
注意力机制 GDN-2 & MLA
激活函数 SwiGLU
精确 bf16
模态 Text

快速入门

Any device with transformers:

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu"
repo = "ArsalanZ/Nenya-2.5B-A0.5B-Base"
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo, trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(repo, trust_remote_code=True, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(device)

inputs = tok("The mitochondrion is the organelle responsible for", return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=40)     # samples: temperature 0.9, top-k 20 (the default)
print(tok.decode(out[0], skip_special_tokens=True))

# maths, code and short factual answers: greedy decoding
out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=40, do_sample=False)

Any device with PyPI

Install it with pip install "nenya[cuda]" on NVIDIA GPUs to get the flash-linear-attention kernels and pip install "nenya" otherwise. With the pip package, trust_remote_code is not needed:

import torch
import nenya                                    # registers the model with transformers
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu"
repo = "ArsalanZ/Nenya-2.5B-A0.5B-Base"
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(repo, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(device)

On a Mac with Apple silicon, use the Metal engine for maximum throughput:

pip install "nenya[mac]"

import nenya
print(nenya.generate("The mitochondrion is the organelle responsible for", max_new_tokens=40))
print(nenya.generate("Question: What is the capital of Australia?\nAnswer:", max_new_tokens=8, temperature=0))

It runs on the Mac's GPU, about 125 tok/s on an M4, and downloads its 3.5 GB weight file on first use. It samples with the model's defaults (temperature 0.9, top-k 20); temperature=0 is greedy decoding, for maths, code and short factual answers.

  • Kernels: on NVIDIA GPUs, install flash-linear-attention (the cuda extra, or pip install flash-linear-attention) so the GDN-2 layers run on its Triton kernels. Without it, on a CPU, or through transformers on a Mac, they run a pure-PyTorch recurrence: same results, much slower, especially on long prompts.
  • Precision: use bf16, as it was trained and evaluated in. fp32 also works.

评估

Pretraining Benchmarks

Scored with lm-evaluation-harness 0.4.13 through transformers (--model hf), from log-likelihoods only: no task generates text. Every model runs with the same settings:

  • bf16 weights, fp32 log-softmax, 4,096-token windows
  • zero-shot except TriviaQA (5-shot, otherwise Qwen's think token invalidates results), lm-eval's default seeds
  • the reference models at their pinned commits

Our training data was decontaminated against these benchmarks' evaluation sets.

Four tasks are ours, and their files are in this repo under evaluation/lm_eval_tasks:

  • mmlu_cloze: lm-eval's 57 mmlu_*_continuation tasks, grouped so that the pooled acc_norm is reported. The stock group reports only acc.
  • csqa_cloze
  • triviaqa_5shot_greedy
  • uncheatable_2026_07

Accuracies are in %, ± one standard error.

Verify our results

The custom task files ship in this repo. On a CUDA GPU:

# our runs: torch 2.11.0+cu128 on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, datasets 5.0.1, huggingface_hub 1.33.0
pip install "lm-eval[hf]==0.4.13" "transformers==5.18.0" "torch==2.11.0" "flash-linear-attention==0.5.2" \
    "datasets==5.0.1"
hf download ArsalanZ/Nenya-2.5B-A0.5B-Base --include "evaluation/*" --local-dir nenya_eval
TASKS=nenya_eval/evaluation/lm_eval_tasks
ARGS=pretrained=ArsalanZ/Nenya-2.5B-A0.5B-Base,trust_remote_code=True,dtype=bfloat16,softmax_dtype=float32,max_length=4096
lm_eval --model hf --model_args $ARGS --include_path $TASKS --output_path results \
    --batch_size 32 --tasks hellaswag,arc_easy,arc_challenge,winogrande,piqa,sciq,openbookqa,lambada_openai,xstorycloze_en,csqa_cloze
lm_eval --model hf --model_args $ARGS --include_path $TASKS --output_path results \
    --batch_size 16 --tasks mmlu_cloze
lm_eval --model hf --model_args $ARGS --include_path $TASKS --output_path results \
    --batch_size 32 --tasks triviaqa_5shot_greedy
lm_eval --model hf --model_args $ARGS --include_path $TASKS --output_path results \
    --batch_size 2 --tasks uncheatable_2026_07

To score a reference model, set ARGS to its arguments below followed by ,dtype=bfloat16,softmax_dtype=float32,max_length=4096. Qwen3.5, Gemma 4 and SmolLM3 ran at half these batch sizes (their vocabularies are 128k–262k tokens). bf16 scores can move slightly with the GPU and the batch size.

局限性

  • A base model. It continues text, it does not follow instructions, and it can produce false, biased or unsafe content.
  • Trained mostly on English web, educational, academic, code and maths data.
  • Quality past 16,384 tokens is untested. With no positional encoding there is no hard limit.
